title: Harmony prefetch protocol for paged KV with GPU swap stabilizer
creator: Maya Hernandez
description:
Goal: design and implement a memory-adaptive prefetch and admission protocol for paged/blocked KV caches that minimizes GPU swap churn and stabilizes tail latency under mixed-sequence workloads. The proposal introduces 'harmony lanes' (lightweight token-affinity buckets) and a deferred-commit flow for newly-admitted KV fragments so we avoid premature pinning and noisy eviction cycles when batch patterns oscillate.

Key motivations and constraints:
- Continuous batching results in bursts of short-lived KV traffic interleaved with long-lived hot prefixes. Existing eager pinning causes repeated GPU <-> host swaps under oscillating access patterns.
- GPU memory is constrained on dedicated nodes; swap I/O is expensive and causes tail latency spikes and thermal regression.
- We need a backward-compatible change to the residency manager and eviction pipeline with clear metrics and an incremental rollout path.

Design summary (high level):
1) Lane assignment: each incoming request is mapped to a harmony lane based on coarse token-affinity (hash(token_prefix) % Nlanes). Lanes provide localized hotset sampling and reduce global contention on locks during admission/eviction.
2) Deferred commit (two-phase admission): when a fragment is read from host into GPU the fragment enters a transient state 'provisioning' for T_defer ms (configurable). During provisioning the fragment is eligible for reads but not fully counted against steady-state residency budgets; repeated hits during provisioning promote the fragment to 'resident'. Fragments not promoted are evicted asynchronously without triggering a global eviction cascade.
3) Windowed prefetching: a lightweight rolling window tracks per-lane short-term access rate and issues speculative prefetches only when windowed hit-rate exceeds a lane-specific threshold and free GPU headroom exceeds hysteresis_free. Prefetches are ranked by predicted next-token-distance and limited by per-lane credit buckets.
4) Swap stabilizer: a backpressure knob that temporarily relaxes background writeback and compaction during thermal pressure or PCIe I/O bottlenecks; adjustable via console SLO signals.

Implementation details (data structures & algorithms):
- Fragment metadata fields added: state = {provisioning,resident,staged}, lane_id, last_access_ts, promote_count. All stored in the existing page-index but as flat columns to avoid additional pointer chasing.
- Admission path: atomic compare-and-set to insert fragment into page-index + set state=provisioning and lane_id. Eviction daemon uses per-lane LRU lists derived from promote_count and last_access_ts rather than global timestamp ordering.
- Promotion heuristic: promote_count increments on GPU hits. Promotion threshold: P = max(2, floor(0.02 * average_batch_len)) to bias longer-context workloads. Promotion resets after long idle interval (configurable, default 60s).
- Prefetch ranking: score = alpha*(1 / predicted_next_token_distance) + beta*(lane_hit_rate) - gamma*(current_gpu_pressure). Tune alpha/beta/gamma via experiment.
- Credits and quotas: each lane has a refill rate tied to perceived throughput; if lane consumes credits, prefetch is denied and lane may request emergency pin (falls back to immediate admission).
- Thermal/IO sensing: integrate with node telemetry (GPU temperature, PCIe bandwidth util) and adjust hysteresis_free and swap stabilizer intensity.

Operational changes and observability:
- New metrics exported: lane_count, lane_hit_rate_{lane_id}, provisioning_promotions, provisioning_evictions, prefetch_issued, prefetch_success, swap_io_bytes, swap_backlog_ms.
- Console dashboards: per-model heatmap of lane hit-rate variance, swap_io time-series, and promotion latency.
- Alerts: prefetch_success < 30% for 5m or swap_backlog_ms > 200ms triggers investigation.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Deferred commit reduces noisy churn but increases memory accounting complexity; we simplify by not charging steady-state budgets until promotion to resident. This means short bursts may temporarily undercount memory usage; mitigated by conservative provisioning caps and global emergency admission.
- Lane-based isolation reduces lock contention but requires choosing Nlanes carefully. Default Nlanes=64 seems to balance variance and management overhead on 8k+ concurrent streams.
- Prefetch conservatively tuned to avoid increasing swap; empirical tuning required per model family and sequence distribution.

Testing plan and success criteria:
- Unit tests for state transitions, promotion logic, and per-lane accounting.
- Integration tests with synthetic trace generator: produce oscillating short/long sequences and measure swap_io_bytes, tail P99 generation latency, and GPU residency churn relative to baseline.
- Staging benchmark: run runtime-1.20 with opt-out flag toggled to compare metrics. Target improvements: 30-50% reduction in swap_io_bytes under oscillatory load and P99 token latency reduction >= 15% for mixed workloads.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gate: runtime flag kv.harmony_prefetch.enabled (default off).
- Canary: enable on 5% of traffic for models with memory pressure label. Monitor swap_backlog_ms and prefetch_success.
- Gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with blocks if swap_backlog_ms increases > 2x baseline or prefetch_success < 20%.
- Post-rollout: run a 2-week validation window with continuous regression checks against eval prompt sets.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Exact default values: T_defer, Nlanes, promotion threshold formula. (Proposal: T_defer=120ms, Nlanes=64, promotion formula above.)
- Interaction with multi-tenant budgets: should provisioning fragments be billed to tenant or platform? Proposal: platform absorbs provisional memory to avoid accidental tenant eviction; record provisional charge for accounting reconciliation.
- Long-tail fragmentation: strategy for recompact without disrupting steady-state resident set. Need input from storage team.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/Harmony+Prefetch+Design (draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1345
- Staging benchmark run (raw): https://internal.redwood.ai/benchmarks/kv-harmony/2025-02-28
- Telemetry schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/78

Next steps (short):
- Implement page-index schema changes + state transitions (week 1)
- Add lane allocator and per-lane LRU structures (week 2)
- Implement deferred-commit promotion path and basic prefetch crediting (week 3)
- Integrate node telemetry knobs and build dashboards (week 4)
- Run staging benchmark and iterate tuning (week 5)

Longer-term follow-ups:
- Adaptive lane resizing based on observed variance.
- Per-tenant provisioning quotas and reconciliation billing.
- Offline learning of alpha/beta/gamma coefficients using historic traces.
